currentContext.business: Incorporated in 1993 in Bangalore, the Company manufactures hard gelatin capsules, HPMC vegetarian capsules and a range of specialty and regulatory capsule variants, supplied to pharmaceutical and nutraceutical customers in India and abroad from facilities at Bangalore and Puducherry. Through its subsidiary Natural Biogenex Private Limited it operates a greenfield facility at Tumkur that manufactures complex steroidal active pharmaceutical ingredients using fermentation-based synthesis from key starting materials, a vertical that reached commercial production during FY26. The two verticals sit in a single value chain: the Company now makes both the active molecule and the capsule that can carry it, an integration it describes as unusual in the Indian industry and central to how it intends to compete.

Capsules: Specialty variants - shiny capsules, sweet capsules, fast-release capsules
Regulatory variants - SLS-free, preservative-free and TSE-free capsules

currentContext.strengths: Backward integration across the value chain - the only backward-integrated producer of select steroidal APIs in India, making both the active molecule and the capsule that carries it|Second-largest Indian manufacturer of gelatin capsules and first company in India to manufacture vegetarian capsules|Dual gelatin and HPMC capability across specialty and regulatory variants, addressing the faster-growing vegetarian/plant-based format|Durable customer relationships - 79.89% repeat business and 32.89% of customers held for more than five years as on 31 March 2026|Export reach across more than 28 countries and five continents, with 28.94% of FY26 revenue from exports|Quality and accreditation base (WHO-GMP, ISO 9001:2015, HACCP, Halal) supporting supply into regulated and emerging markets|More than three decades of manufacturing experience and in-house patented technology for its steroidal API molecules|First three API molecules covered by the Government of India's Production Linked Incentive scheme|Investment in next-generation capsule manufacturing equipment delivering higher output, lower per-unit labour cost, better energy efficiency, shorter cycles and lower rejection rates
currentContext.strategies: Expanding reach in regulated markets - deepening relationships with high-volume buyers and pursuing new geographies for the gelatin and HPMC capsule range|Driving innovation in capsule offerings - developing new capsule variants for evolving market needs, supported by next-generation manufacturing technology and process innovation|Enhancing manufacturing efficiency - investing in advanced technologies and processes to optimise productivity and cost across both capsule sites|Accelerating ramp-up of the API facility - stabilising commercial production at Tumkur, building utilisation and progressing towards the certifications required for regulated export markets|Ensuring margin stability - strengthening relationships with high-volume buyers and improving the mix towards higher-value products to reduce volatility and support margins|Strengthening the API portfolio - advancing the steroidal API range and pursuing new molecules through ongoing investment in research and development|Upholding regulatory excellence - maintaining stringent quality management systems to secure and sustain regulatory approvals and support long-term customer relationships|Lifting utilisation across both capsule sites and deepening long-standing customer relationships now that the Puducherry disruption is resolved|Holding to a stated operating discipline: manufacture in-house, integrate where it genuinely adds value, and invest through cycles rather than only in favourable years
currentContext.expansion: FY26 completed a multi-year build-out across three units and two businesses. In the capsule business the Company commissioned a new HPMC line for double-zero capsules during the year, taking installed capsule capacity to 20.25 BCPA as on 31 March 2026, and continued to invest in next-generation hard-capsule manufacturing equipment that raises output, adds automation with lower per-unit labour cost, improves energy efficiency and shortens production cycles. One further HPMC capsule unit is still to be installed at the Bangalore unit, which the Board says is expected to be completed in financial year 2026-27. The greenfield API facility at Tumkur, operated through the subsidiary Natural Biogenex Private Limited, moved from construction into commercial production in FY26 after being fully capitalised and running commercial batches in FY25; it makes complex steroidal APIs by fermentation-based synthesis, with the first three molecules (Dexamethasone, Betamethasone and Prednisolone) approved under the Production Linked Incentive scheme, and it is being developed in alignment with international regulatory requirements while certification is still being pursued. In the fourth quarter the Company signed a framework and contract manufacturing agreement with FermBox Bio, an arrangement intended to bring additional utilisation to Tumkur. Capacity growth has been long-running: operations began with three lines and 1.03 billion capsules a year, nine lines were acquired from Qualicaps Canada and five from IPCL Godhra and installed at Pondicherry, individual line capacities were raised from 1.0 to 1.5 million capsules a day (and one line to 2.5 million a day), and installed capacity had reached 7.1 billion capsules per annum by 2014. The stated priorities for the next phase are operational rather than new-build: restoring and lifting utilisation across the capsule sites after the Puducherry licensing shutdown was resolved, and building volumes at the API facility. Expansion is being funded from internal accruals - the Board withheld a dividend for 2025-26 citing the need to conserve internal accruals for capacity expansion - and the parent has extended corporate guarantees to the subsidiary Natural Biogenex Private Limited under section 186 of the Companies Act, 2013.
currentContext.mdna: Demand for HPMC/vegetarian capsules continues to build as pharmaceutical and nutraceutical customers shift towards plant-based and liquid-fill formats; HPMC and pullulan capsules are the faster-growing part of the global empty-capsules market, expanding at a compound annual rate of around 10% against gelatin's majority revenue share of around 66% in 2025|Oral solid-dose forms (tablets and capsules) remain the dominant means of delivering medicine, keeping capsule demand closely tied to growth of the pharmaceutical industry as a whole|Nutraceutical and wellness consumption is a particular engine of growth, with the Indian nutraceuticals segment growing at double-digit rates and chronic-therapy segments such as cardiac, gastrointestinal and anti-diabetic growing at around 9% to 10% a year|Global supply-chain diversification away from single-source dependence for active ingredients is directing fresh attention and investment towards Indian API producers, with an estimated 65% to 70% of key intermediates still sourced from China|Tightening regulatory oversight and site inspection rewards producers combining compliant manufacturing with the ability to make complex, higher-value molecules - the space the Company says its API business occupies|Government policy continuity (Production Linked Incentive scheme, Bulk Drug Parks programme, Make in India) supports domestic API manufacturing and import substitution, a direction management says aligns with the Company's own backward integration|Margin lever from mix: for manufacturers able to offer both gelatin and HPMC across a range of specifications, widening demand is an opportunity to move beyond commodity supply towards higher-value, differentiated products|Cost headwind flagged: the cost and availability of imported raw materials such as gelatin and HPMC, which are subject to price movement and can affect production costs and margins|The API market remains competitive with pressure on global realisations, so the near-term task is stabilising production, building utilisation and securing certifications rather than price-led growth|Earnings drag in FY26 was attributed to an identifiable, largely non-recurring Puducherry disruption plus front-loaded costs of newly commissioned capacity, rather than erosion of the underlying capsule business|Demand in export markets held up, particularly for HPMC capsules, where the shift towards vegetarian and plant-based formats continued to support order flow|Long-standing customer relationships, many of them spanning years, gave the capsule business a stable base from which to absorb the year's disruption and recover through its closing months

risks.risk: Site licensing and regulatory permission risk at manufacturing facilities
risks.note: A licensing matter at the Puducherry capsule facility led to a temporary shutdown that disrupted production and dispatches for part of FY26 and was the principal drag on volumes. The licence position was resolved during the year, but the episode shows how a single permission issue at one of only three units can interrupt output while fixed costs continue.

risks.risk: Raw-material cost and availability, particularly gelatin and HPMC
risks.note: Management identifies the supply and cost of raw materials such as gelatin and HPMC, which are often imported and subject to price movement, as an enduring challenge that can affect production costs and margins.

risks.risk: Import dependence for key starting materials and intermediates
risks.note: An estimated 65% to 70% of key intermediates for the Indian API industry are still sourced from China, exposing the sector to supply-chain and price risk. This is the very dependence the Company's backward integration is designed to reduce, but the starting-material chain remains a structural exposure.

risks.risk: Pricing pressure and competition in the global API market
risks.note: The API business, in its first year of commercial production, operated against global pricing pressure while establishing customer connections, and the market is marked by geographic concentration and a shift in competition towards complex, higher-value molecules.

risks.risk: Execution and ramp-up risk on newly commissioned capacity
risks.note: The full-year cost of depreciation and finance charges on newly commissioned capacity arrived at a stage when revenue from the newer platforms was still building. Returns depend on restoring and lifting utilisation across the capsule sites and building volumes in the API business.

risks.risk: Pending regulatory certification for the API facility
risks.note: The Tumkur facility is still working towards regulatory certification; until it is obtained, access to regulated export markets - and therefore the facility's addressable market - remains limited. Global authorities are also intensifying inspection of manufacturing sites and enforcing environmental and quality standards.

risks.risk: Extension of the control environment to a second, more complex manufacturing operation
risks.note: Commissioning the API facility extended the control environment to an operation with its own requirements for process safety, quality documentation and environmental compliance; bringing it within the established framework of authorisation, review and audit remains a focus as the facility scales.

risks.risk: Contingent exposure to the subsidiary through corporate guarantees
risks.note: The Company has given corporate guarantees to its subsidiary Natural Biogenex Private Limited under section 186 of the Companies Act, 2013, so the parent carries contingent exposure to the performance of the API business.

thesis (one line): Cash-generating gelatin-capsule core (~93% utilization) is funding a heavily loss-making, debt-funded API ramp (Tumkur/NBPL); FY26 was a write-off year (Puducherry shutdown + pre-commercial API costs); FY27 thesis hinges on (a) HPMC line approval/utilization, (b) API moving up the regulatory ladder to escape thin generic margins, and (c) restoring consolidated profitability — but balance-sheet/liquidity stress is real and fundraising is being pursued.
scorecard: Puducherry capsule plant temporary shutdown → ~Rs.6 cr deferred dispatches cleared in Q4 FY26 (mfg cost already absorbed in Q3 → higher net realization aided Q4 margin recovery).
API subsidiary (NBPL) pre-commercial cost burden: mfg costs + fixed overheads with negligible revenue most of the year; commercial API sales only began Q4 FY26 (~Rs.9 cr in Q4).
Depreciation FY26 Rs.17.14 cr (vs Rs.9.12 cr) — Tumkur API assets entered depreciation cycle.
Operating cash flow FY26 POSITIVE Rs.10.92 cr (capsule business cash generation). Total equity Rs.234.72 cr.
guidance (critical — fy27): Consolidated revenue target ~Rs.274 cr for FY27, built up as:
Gelatin capsules: ~Rs.170 cr (FY26 actual ~Rs.163 cr; would have been ~Rs.170 cr ex Pondicherry shutdown loss of ~Rs.6 cr). Assumed EBITDA margin ~13%. Util >93%.

HPMC capsules: ~Rs.20 cr (vs earlier-stated Rs.25 cr ambition; FY26 actual only ~Rs.8 cr, of which ~Rs.3 cr US, stopped after ~July). Assumed EBITDA margin ~18%. Capacity 1.5 bn capsules (2 lines × 750 mn); FY27 util assumed <50% due to US uncertainty. New "double zero" size, ready for US but pending customer machine-suitability/stability approvals → revenue expected H2 FY27.

API (NBPL, domestic): ~Rs.70 cr (called ~Rs.70–84 cr across the call; based on Q4 ~Rs.9 cr run-rate + gradual increase). Gross margin only ~2–3%; EBITDA likely still NEGATIVE / negligible-low-single-digit. No PLI revenue included in guidance.
Fermbox CMO contract: ~Rs.14 cr (one confirmed Govt-of-India product); EBITDA ~20% per agreed cost sheet.
Consol FY27: management warns "very low consolidated net margin" / may "face challenges"; restoring consol profitability is the primary FY27 financial target.
Medium-term API revenue target Rs.240–250 cr retained but pushed to ~2–3 years (FY29); needs ~Rs.25–30 cr more capex for 2 additional clean rooms.
demand / pipeline: Capsule order book backlog ~36 days across all capsule types.

US Neutra/wellness capsule demand "completely slowed down" post US tariffs (50% India-specific tariff + anti-dumping); expected to improve in 3–6 months. HPMC samples sent to US customers; awaiting machine-suitability + stability testing (2–3 months).
HPMC export pivot to Brazil, Mexico (improved); intend to start Europe (organic + veterinary gelatin registrations obtained).

API: domestic generic demand exists but highly price-sensitive (single-digit-low EBITDA). Target regulated/semi-regulated customers (Cipla, Lupin, Mankind; exports US/EU/Japan via Korea route) post WHO GMP.
segment (capsules vs api): Capsules (core, profitable): Gelatin ~Rs.163–170 cr, >93% util, 12–13% EBITDA margin (peaked 20–22% in COVID FY21–23). HPMC nascent, ~18% margin, US-export dependent and currently stalled.

API (NBPL/Tumkur, loss-making): Commercial sales began Q4 FY26 (~Rs.9 cr). Util ~25–30%. End-to-end from base RM (Phytosterol) — claims to be only non-China end-to-end maker for these steroidals. Generic margins thin; profitability needs regulatory upgrade.

Fermbox CMO (new): Uses ~40% spare fermentation capacity (freed because sanctioned API capacity < applied, and enzymatic route reduced fermentation need). Fermbox invests ~Rs.60 cr in equipment (on NCL site, owned by Fermbox), provides tech/strains/supervision; NCL does ground ops + gets revenue share. No-compete clause. Could scale to Rs.50 cr+ over 2–3 yrs.
growth / optionality: HPMC veg-capsule mix shift (higher margin, regulated markets, US double-zero approval) — biggest near-term capsule lever; full 1.5 bn util → ~Rs.45 cr HPMC rev → ~+200 bps weighted EBITDA margin.
API up-the-ladder: WHO GMP (targeted Q2 FY27), CEP filing, USFDA (~Q3/Q4 FY27 / 24 months) → access to regulated/export customers with materially better margins.

PLI optionality (NOT in guidance): Prednisolone & Dexamethasone achieved at kilo level (~10% above Chinese cost); Govt minimum-import-price (MIP) precedent set for Kinwa & Aurobindo products. Chartered-engineer visit done; technical team visit expected 3–4 months; Betamethasone targeted Q4 FY27.
Government RDI/BIRAC deep-tech funding application pending (would need matching equity).
China+1 / supply-chain security: US & Japan companies "eager to tie up" subject to regulatory clearances.
margins & cost (incl. gelatin cost): Gelatin EBITDA ~12–13%, helped by rupee depreciation (better dollar recoveries). HPMC ~18% (5% delta over gelatin).
API gross only 2–3%; EBITDA breakeven NOT achievable at current customer mix even at 100% util — depends on customer quality/geography, not utilization.

China steroidal-API overcapacity depresses Indian prices (India prices lowest globally, may not cover Chinese cost). Recent RM/intermediate price spikes from Iran-US war / petroleum. China export rebate reduced but offset by Yuan depreciation.
API fixed cost burden ~Rs.1–1.25 cr/month (~Rs.15 cr/annum).
capex: New HPMC line commissioned FY26 (capacity 19.5 → 25 bn capsules).
API clean rooms: ~Rs.25–30 cr more needed for 2 additional clean rooms to reach Rs.250 cr API target (FY29); basic infrastructure already built.
Fermbox equipment ~Rs.60 cr funded by Fermbox (off NCL balance sheet). Any future fermentation expansion for Fermbox = separate new facility/capex.
capital allocation: Liquidity/balance-sheet stress acknowledged ("near-zero cash balance"). Consol debt ~Rs.100–110 cr, guided flat FY27/FY28; may add ~Rs.20 cr over 2 yrs; repayments Rs.10–12 cr/yr.
Fundraising options under review: BIRAC/RDI grant + matching equity; possible preferential allotment (promoters may participate); possible rights issue. Promoters do NOT want to dilute holding much.
PE claw-back clause in NBPL is tied to FY29 (not FY27) targets per shareholders' agreement — no current discussion.
risks: Liquidity / near-zero cash; reliance on dilution or grants; persistent consol losses.

API margins structurally thin until regulatory upgrades (WHO GMP/CEP/USFDA) land — repeated timeline slippages (FY24–FY26 guidance misses; Q4 FY26 cash-breakeven guided earlier, only commercial sales started).
US tariff/anti-dumping + Neutra-demand slump hurting HPMC exports; recovery uncertain.
China steroidal overcapacity & dumping into India; intermediate price volatility (Iran-US war).
Execution stretch: 5 concurrent strategic priorities (gelatin scale, HPMC regulated, API commercial ramp, fermentation qualification, Fermbox) on a stressed balance sheet.
PLI/MIP benefit timing uncertain (excluded from guidance, so upside not downside).
management tone: Candid and contrite on FY26 ("must be candid… deterioration of 1,119 bps"; acknowledges repeated misses). Guidance explicitly framed as conservative (no PLI, low US/HPMC assumptions). Optimistic medium-term ("future is bright", "only company outside China end-to-end"). Realistic on near-term consol margins being "very low."
non-obvious: Q4 margin recovery partly artificial: ~Rs.6 cr deferred Puducherry dispatches carried abnormally high realization (mfg cost already booked in Q3) — not a clean run-rate.
API breakeven is a customer-mix problem, not a volume problem — even 100% util at current customers won't break even.

Fermentation capacity became "spare" because DoP clarified produce-sanctioned-not-applied capacity (Dexa/Beta committed 27 MT vs allotted 8 → 19 MT freed) + enzymatic route cut fermentation need → enabled Fermbox monetization.

Govt has blocked publication of export/import data (data only to Dec); FY26 import benchmarks partial. Import benchmarks cited: Prednisolone ~40 MT @ ~$230/kg; Dexamethasone ~50 MT @ ~$350/kg; Betamethasone ~25 MT @ ~$580/kg.
Chinese routing anti-dumping via Colombia etc.; ACG ($100m) and others' US-plant plans now "in cold shelf."
Strides supplies prednisolone to Pfizer (~8 MT); Dr Reddy's Abiraterone Acetate — illustrates the regulated-export volume pool NCL targets.
challenges → beneficiaries (✅ / ⭐): US tariffs + Neutra slowdown hurting NCL HPMC exports ✅ (China-routing players via 3rd countries; domestic/Brazil/Mexico capsule suppliers).
Steroidal API import-substitution + MIP/PLI policy ⭐ potential beneficiary = Natural Capsules itself (only non-China end-to-end claimant) + Aurobindo, Kinwa (already got MIP precedents).
China steroidal overcapacity ✅ Indian formulators buying cheap API; ❌ for domestic API makers like NCL.
qoq log: Q4 FY26 (this call): Revenue Rs.58.45 cr (+55% QoQ, +30% YoY); EBITDA Rs.1.33 cr / 2.28% (helped by Rs.6 cr high-realization deferred Puducherry sales). FY26 EBITDA loss Rs.1.56 cr; net loss Rs.24.66 cr. Capacity now 25 bn capsules (new HPMC line ready, awaiting US approval, rev H2 FY27). Commercial API sales began (~Rs.9 cr Q4). Fermbox CMO signed (~Rs.60 cr Fermbox equip; ~Rs.14 cr FY27 rev). FY27 guidance ~Rs.274 cr consol (Gelatin 170 / HPMC 20 / API 70 / Fermbox 14). Debt ~Rs.100–110 cr. Primary FY27 goal = restore consol profitability. Fundraising (BIRAC + pref/rights) under consideration.
Prior-quarter context referenced: Q3 FY26 = Puducherry shutdown, deferred dispatches, EBITDA much weaker (~Rs.0.5 cr implied). FY25 baseline: Rev Rs.169.21 cr, EBITDA Rs.17.52 cr / 10.35%.

US tariff/anti-dumping + Neutra-demand slump hurting HPMC exports; recovery uncertain.
China steroidal overcapacity & dumping into India; intermediate price volatility (Iran-US war).
Execution stretch: 5 concurrent strategic priorities (gelatin scale, HPMC regulated, API commercial ramp, fermentation qualification, Fermbox) on a stressed balance sheet.
PLI/MIP benefit timing uncertain (excluded from guidance, so upside not downside).
management tone: Candid and contrite on FY26 ("must be candid… deterioration of 1,119 bps"; acknowledges repeated misses). Guidance explicitly framed as conservative (no PLI, low US/HPMC assumptions). Optimistic medium-term ("future is bright", "only company outside China end-to-end"). Realistic on near-term consol margins being "very low."
non-obvious: Q4 margin recovery partly artificial: ~Rs.6 cr deferred Puducherry dispatches carried abnormally high realization (mfg cost already booked in Q3) — not a clean run-rate.
API breakeven is a customer-mix problem, not a volume problem — even 100% util at current customers won't break even.

Fermentation capacity became "spare" because DoP clarified produce-sanctioned-not-applied capacity (Dexa/Beta committed 27 MT vs allotted 8 → 19 MT freed) + enzymatic route cut fermentation need → enabled Fermbox monetization.

Govt has blocked publication of export/import data (data only to Dec); FY26 import benchmarks partial. Import benchmarks cited: Prednisolone ~40 MT @ ~$230/kg; Dexamethasone ~50 MT @ ~$350/kg; Betamethasone ~25 MT @ ~$580/kg.
Chinese routing anti-dumping via Colombia etc.; ACG ($100m) and others' US-plant plans now "in cold shelf."
Strides supplies prednisolone to Pfizer (~8 MT); Dr Reddy's Abiraterone Acetate — illustrates the regulated-export volume pool NCL targets.
challenges → beneficiaries (✅ / ⭐): US tariffs + Neutra slowdown hurting NCL HPMC exports ✅ (China-routing players via 3rd countries; domestic/Brazil/Mexico capsule suppliers).
Steroidal API import-substitution + MIP/PLI policy ⭐ potential beneficiary = Natural Capsules itself (only non-China end-to-end claimant) + Aurobindo, Kinwa (already got MIP precedents).
China steroidal overcapacity ✅ Indian formulators buying cheap API; ❌ for domestic API makers like NCL.
qoq log: Q4 FY26 (this call): Revenue Rs.58.45 cr (+55% QoQ, +30% YoY); EBITDA Rs.1.33 cr / 2.28% (helped by Rs.6 cr high-realization deferred Puducherry sales). FY26 EBITDA loss Rs.1.56 cr; net loss Rs.24.66 cr. Capacity now 25 bn capsules (new HPMC line ready, awaiting US approval, rev H2 FY27). Commercial API sales began (~Rs.9 cr Q4). Fermbox CMO signed (~Rs.60 cr Fermbox equip; ~Rs.14 cr FY27 rev). FY27 guidance ~Rs.274 cr consol (Gelatin 170 / HPMC 20 / API 70 / Fermbox 14). Debt ~Rs.100–110 cr. Primary FY27 goal = restore consol profitability. Fundraising (BIRAC + pref/rights) under consideration.
Prior-quarter context referenced: Q3 FY26 = Puducherry shutdown, deferred dispatches, EBITDA much weaker (~Rs.0.5 cr implied). FY25 baseline: Rev Rs.169.21 cr, EBITDA Rs.17.52 cr / 10.35%.

themes.title: Pharma US complex-generics & specialty exports
themes.need: US complex generics, Para-IV FTFs and the GLP-1/semaglutide wave still drive export pharma, but Q1FY27 delivered one hard setback and one deliberate trough. DRREDDY held an out-of-cycle call disclosing a semaglutide injectable API scale-up validation failure - an out-of-spec impurity in finished product - halting supply through roughly September and re-cutting FY27 volumes to 6-7 million pens (Q3-Q4) from an earlier ~12mn first-year target, which re-times India's largest semaglutide launch and opens a share window for rivals. CIPLA let EBITDA margin fall to 16.7%, below the pre-Revlimid level, because launch opex is committed ahead of revenue plus ~1-2% of revenue in war-related input cost - yet reaffirmed BOTH an FY27 18.5-20% margin and a $1bn US exit run-rate off a $162m Q1, making this a trough by design with unusually large operating leverage if the launches land. The GLP-1 opportunity is bifurcating: CIPLA's Yurpeak (tirzepatide, Eli Lilly collaboration) did INR 80cr and is already the #2 anti-obesity brand behind Mounjaro while Cipla deliberately sits out the crowded semaglutide-generic price war. NATCOPHARM remains in a gRevlimid post-cliff base year; LUPIN/ALKEM/ZYDUSLIFE/LAURUSLABS carry cleaner momentum; SENORES/MARKSANS on US generics; DIVISLAB on GLP-1 peptides (55% CDMO mix).
themes.driver: DRREDDY's semaglutide supply restart (guided ~September) and whether the 6-7mn-pen re-cut holds; CIPLA's four US launches landing against the reaffirmed 18.5-20% FY27 margin; FTF launches and USFDA clearances; DIVISLAB Kakinada Unit 3 from FY27.

themes.title: Pharma CDMO / CRDMO & API import-substitution
themes.need: Global biopharma's China+1 sourcing plus a peptide/biologics modality boom drive India's CDMO/CRDMO build-out and API import-substitution. ANTHEM/COHANCE/NEULANDLAB/SYNGENE-tier on CRDMO (peptides/ADCs/oligos); DIVISLAB/LAURUSLABS on peptide CDMO; AKUMS/INNOVACAP/RUBICON on formulation CDMO; AARTIPHARM/SUPRIYA/AARTIDRUGS/SOLARA on APIs; SIGACHI/NATCAPSUQ/VIDHIING on excipients.
themes.driver: Customer regulatory filings unlocking dedicated capacity; new CRDMO molecule wins; API price/volume recovery.
